sentences.text: JUDGMENT

The plaintiff has instituted the present suit seeking recovery of a sum of 6,00,000/-, being the refundable security deposit paid to defendant No.1 under a lease agreement, along with interest at the rate of 18% per annum from the date of filing the suit until realization.

The succinct narrative of the plaintiffs' contention is as follows:
The plaintiff has contended that defendant No.1 leased the residential premises constructed on property bearing No. 3075, PID No. 55-303-3075, located near Water Tank, 4th Cross, 5th Main, 1st Stage, Kumarswamy Layout, Bengaluru - 78, more fully described as schedule 'A' property in the plaint, and the residential premises described as schedule 'B' property in the plaint (hereinafter referred to as the suit 'A'
and 'B' schedule properties) to the plaintiff on lease, receiving a refundable security deposit of 6,00,000/-.
The plaintiff and defendant No.1 entered into a Lease Agreement dated 01.01.2019, through which the 'B' schedule property was leased to the plaintiff for a period of two years.

However, on 18.01.2021, the plaintiff received a notice from defendant No.2, Bangalore City Co-op. Bank Ltd., Padmanabhanagar Branch, Bengaluru, informing that the suit 'A' schedule property had been mortgaged in favor of the Bank for a loan.

Due to defendant No.1's default, the Bank had Mohammed Nadim vs Janardhana M on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40089546/
2 initiated proceedings under the Securitization and Cont'd..
-4- O.S. No.5514/2021 Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, and the constructive possession of the building was taken by the Bank through a notice dated 16.03.2020.

entities.text: Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The plaintiff immediately inquired with defendant No.1 regarding this issue, but defendant No.1 claimed ignorance.
The plaintiff later learned that defendant No.1 had availed loans of 30,00,000/- and 11,90,000/- from Bangalore City Co-op. Bank Ltd., using the suit 'A' schedule property as mortgage.

However, defendant No.1 did not disclose this fact to the plaintiff before letting out the 'B' schedule property on lease, for which the plaintiff paid 6,00,000/- as security deposit, nor did he inform the plaintiff that the property was mortgaged.
On 21.01.2021, defendant No.2 took physical possession of the leased premises, effectively evicting the plaintiff from the leased property.

Consequently, the plaintiff filed a complaint with Kumarswamy Layout Police, Bengaluru, on 02.09.2021, which led to the registration of an FIR against defendant No.1 for offenses punishable under Sections 405, 420, 504, and 506 of the IPC.

Subsequently,
the Bank sold the 'A' schedule property in an auction for a reserve Cont'd..
-5- O.S. No.5514/2021 price of 54,28,000/-, and a surplus amount of 12,24,443/-
was retained by defendant No.2.
As a result, the plaintiff has filed the present suit seeking recovery of the security deposit of 6,00,000/- paid under the Lease Agreement dated 01.01.2019.

The plaintiff also requests that, in case of default,
defendant No.2 be directed to satisfy the debt to the extent of defendant No.1's liability.
3. Upon service of summons, defendants No.1 and No.2 entered appearance through their respective counsel and filed separate written statements.
Defendant No.1 has disputed the existence of a jural relationship with the plaintiff.

While the written statement filed by defendant No.1 is lengthy, the key points are as follows:
Defendant No.1 claims to be the absolute owner of the suit 'A' schedule property and states that he entered into a Sale Agreement with Sri. K. Babu for the sale of the property for a consideration of 78,00,000/- through a registered Agreement of Sale dated 21.05.2018.

At the time of the agreement, defendant No.1 received 17,00,000/- as an advance, with a Cont'd..
-6- O.S. No.5514/2021 condition to complete the sale transaction within one month.

Subsequently, on 30.07.2018, K. Babu, through his associate Sri. Imtihaiz Pasha,
paid an additional 6,00,000/- and 7,00,000/- from one Smt. Neela towards the sale consideration, bringing the total amount received to 25,00,000/-.

4. Defendant No.1 further contends that after entering into the Agreement of Sale, K. Babu inducted the plaintiff as a tenant in the house situated on the ground floor, Smt. Neela on the first floor, and Jagadish Gowda on the third floor.
Based on instructions from K. Babu, defendant No.1 executed Mohammed Nadim vs Janardhana M on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40089546/
3 Lease Deeds in favor of Smt. Neela and Jagadish Gowda on 12.12.2013 and 13.12.2018, respectively.
However, defendant No.1 claims he did not execute any Lease Deed in favor of the plaintiff.
The Agreement of Sale was later canceled, and defendant No.1 repaid the earnest money to K. Babu via cheque and NEFT.
During this time, defendant No.2 initiated proceedings to recover the loan amount for which the suit 'A' schedule property was mortgaged.

Defendant No.1 disputes the plaintiff's claim of having Cont'd..
-7- O.S. No.5514/2021 paid any lease amount for the suit 'B' schedule property and denies any liability to pay the amount claimed by the plaintiff.
Consequently, defendant No.1 seeks the dismissal of the suit with costs.
5. Defendant No.2, in its written statement, has pleaded ignorance about the transactions between the plaintiff and defendant No.1.
However, defendant No.2 admits that it took steps to recover the loan amount of 24,23,631/- advanced to defendant No.1, for which the suit 'A' schedule property was mortgaged.
Under the provisions of the SARFAESI Act, possession was taken, and the property was sold in a public auction.
Defendant No.2 also executed a Sale Certificate in favor of the auction purchaser on 08.11.2021 in respect of the 'A' schedule property.
6. On the premise of above pleadings, this court has framed the following Issues - ISSUES 1.

Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendant No.1 executed Lease Deed dated: 01.01.2019 in Cont'd..
-8- O.S. No.5514/2021 favour of plaintiff in respect of Leased Premises for a period of 3 years and he has paid Rs.6,00,000/- to him as security deposit?
2. Whether the defendant No.1 proves that the plaintiff is the assignee of Sri.K.Babu, therefore he is not liable to pay any amount to the plaintiff?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the reliefs sought for?
4. What order or decree?
7. In order to substantiate the claim, the plaintiff himself got examined as PW.1 and produced Ex.P.1 to P.5 documents.
The defendants have not challenged the evidence adduced by the plaintiff and even they have not bother to lead any evidence in their defence.
8. I have heard the arguments of plaintiff's counsel and perused the entire evidence adduced by the plaintiff.

sentences.text:
The plaintiff contends that defendant No.1 inducted him as a tenant in respect of the suit 'B'
schedule property through a Lease Agreement dated 01.01.2019, while suppressing the material fact that the entire suit 'A' schedule property was mortgaged in favor of defendant No.2.
The plaintiff further asserts that, due to the default of defendant No.1, defendant No.2 initiated proceedings under the SARFAESI Act to recover the debt.
Consequently, the suit 'A' schedule property was taken over by defendant No.2 and sold in a public auction, a fact that is not disputed by any party.

The plaintiff has produced the Lease Agreement dated 01.01.2019 as per Ex.P.1, a notice issued by defendant No.2 on 01.10.2021 to the plaintiff as per Ex.P.2, and a notice dated 18.01.2021 as per Ex.P.3, demanding the vacation of the suit 'B' schedule property within seven days.

Additionally,
Ex.P.4 is the notice dated 13.10.2021 issued by defendant No.2, further demanding that the plaintiff vacate the premises.
These documents clearly establish that the plaintiff was in lawful possession of the suit 'B' schedule property as a tenant.

While the defendant No.1 disputes the jural relationship of tenant and landlord, despite being given ample opportunity to present evidence to challenge the plaintiff's claims, the defendant has failed to contest the evidence of PW.1 in any substantial way.
The defendant has not cross-examined the plaintiff's witness or led any rebuttal evidence to dispute the execution of the Lease Deed, Ex.P.1.

Further, despite disputing the Lease Deed's execution, the defendant has not provided any alternative documentary evidence to suggest that the Lease Deed was fabricated or that the plaintiff was not Cont'd..

- 11 O.S. No.5514/2021 inducted into the premises under the terms outlined in Ex.P.1.

sentences.text: In addition, as per the court's order, defendant No.2 deposited a sum of 6,00,000/- from the surplus amount of the auction sale following the plaintiff's application.
This amount is currently held by the court in Fixed Deposit (FD).
While the defendant No.1 has challenged this order, the amount remains in the court's custody pending resolution.

The failure of the defendant to present any evidence to the contrary, combined with the clear documentation presented by the plaintiff,
supports the conclusion that the plaintiff is entitled to the refundable security deposit of 6,00,000/- as outlined in the Lease Agreement Ex.P.1.

It is well established that, where a tenant has paid a refundable security deposit under a valid lease agreement, the landlord is obligated to return the amount at the end of the lease term, barring any outstanding dues.
The defendant's failure to provide evidence undermines any defense against the plaintiff's claim for the return of the deposit.

A tenant's right to Cont'd..
 - 12 O.S. No.5514/2021  claim the refund of the security deposit is not dependent on the landlord's failure to fulfill contractual obligations unless there is evidence of damage or loss to the property.
As no such evidence has been provided by the defendant, the plaintiff's entitlement to the security deposit remains uncontested.

12. In light of these facts, and in the absence of any credible evidence to dispute the plaintiff's case, I find no reason to deny the plaintiff's claim for the return of the 6,00,000/- refundable security deposit.
Additionally, the notices issued by defendant No.2 as per Ex.P.2 to Ex.P.4 further substantiate the plaintiff's possession and tenancy of the 'B' schedule property.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, I am compelled to answer Issues No.1 to 3 in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE No.4 :
For the aforesaid reasons and discussion, I proceed to pass the following - ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is decreed with cost.
Cont'd..

The plaintiff is entitled for refundable security amount of Rs.6,00,000/-
from the defendant No.1 with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from 01.01.2019, till the date of realization.
The defendant No.2 is directed to pay the suit claim from surplus amount of auction sale available with them as a protanto satisfaction.

The amount deposited by the defendant No.2 before this court as per order dated:19.09.2022 and deposited for Fixed Term with Karnataka Bank Limited, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru as per order dated: 29.03.2023 shall be released in favour of plaintiff with accursed interest through e-payment Draw decree accordingly.
